summary: Persistent client-side retry cascade + single-connection pooling from tenant SDKs causing perceived inference slowdowns
description:
Issue summary:
Customer NimbleDocs reported a sharp degradation in perceived inference latency for a subset of endpoints starting 2026-03-09 22:00 UTC. Customer traffic is routed through Redwood hosted API (prod, us-east). The customer is on Dedicated tier with pinned model gptx-3.8-rlhf.

Impact:
- ~30% of requests from the customer's tenant observed >2s added tail latency and ~7% client-side timeouts reported from their monitoring.
- No platform-wide outage; increase concentrated to NimbleDocs' tenant and coincidentally a small group of other customers using the same SDK version.

Environment / context:
- Redwood hosted API (prod, us-east), dedicated capacity pool for customer.
- Customer using redwood-sdk-java v1.4.2 (default HTTP client config).
- Model variants: gptx-3.8-rlhf (primary), gptx-3.8-quant (fallback).
- SDK default connection pool configured with maxConnections=1 per host in this version for legacy compatibility; retry_policy: retry_on_5xx=true, retry_attempts=5, backoff=exponential(base_ms=400) with no jitter by default.

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Send steady stream of chat-completion requests at ~12 qps with concurrent client threads (20 threads) and streaming response enabled.
2) Observe that after ~30s of load, p95 latency climbs and a number of client requests time out (client-side 30s timeout).
3) Restarting client processes temporarily restores normal latencies until load ramps again.

Observed behaviour:
- Server ingestion and per-request processing times remain within normal bounds (per-host token throughput steady).
- Connection metrics show many client connections short-lived; server logs show serialized request arrival bursts from the same client IPs.
- Client-side traces show requests being retried serially due to single-connection pool exhaustion and aggressive retry attempts, amplifying end-to-end latency.

Expected behaviour:
- Client SDK should use connection pooling and non-blocking retries to avoid serialized retries that add to end-to-end latency.

Attached / referenced evidence:
- Customer-provided flamegraphs and trace IDs (redacted) and sample request IDs: RID: 20260309-UE7-8832
- Internal logs indicating connection churn and HTTP 502->retry patterns in front-end load balancer.
- Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/latency/nimbledocs-tenant?from=2026-03-09T21:50:00Z
comments: Support (2026-03-10 04:05 UTC): Opened ticket after NimbleDocs raised alert. Initial triage indicates client-side retry behavior may be amplifying latency. Assigned to SRE + SDK owners.

SRE (Marius Chen) (2026-03-10 05:20 UTC): Correlated tenant's source IP with connection metrics. Observed max_connections_in_use frequently hitting 1 and average request queue length on client side growing. No server-side CPU/GPU saturation observed.

SDK (Leah Ortiz) (2026-03-10 08:45 UTC): Reproduced locally with redwood-sdk-java v1.4.2 using 20 concurrent threads; observed sequentialized retries when pool size=1. Behavior fixed when pool size increased to 8 and retry_attempts reduced to 2 with jitter enabled.

Customer (NimbleDocs - Martin Delaney) (2026-03-10 12:10 UTC): Confirmed temporary mitigation by toggling client config (increased pool size and lower retries), tail latency returned to baseline for the next 3 hours during testing. Asked for recommended long-term fix and whether Redwood will adjust defaults.

Support (2026-03-11 09:00 UTC): Escalated to SDK maintainers to ship a patch and to DX/docs to update quickstart guidance for concurrent workloads and streaming use-cases. Logged follow-up actions below.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 05:00 UTC - SRE: No GPU or node-level degradation in dedicated pool. Serving runtime per-request tokens processed within SLO. Indicates client-side serialization upstream.

2026-03-10 06:15 UTC - Network: Frontend ELB logs show bursts of re-issued requests (retries) from same client IP; request inter-arrival times indicate back-to-back retries rather than independent concurrent requests.

2026-03-10 07:30 UTC - SDK repro: With v1.4.2 defaults, a transient 502 causes up to 5 retry attempts; because pool=maxConnections=1, retries wait on the single connection leading to queuing at client and high client-observed latency.
Change of server health check frequency increased transient 502s by a small margin during rolling maintenance earlier that evening, which triggered retry cascade for affected tenants.

2026-03-10 08:40 UTC - Mitigation test: Adjusting SDK to maxConnections=8, retry_attempts=2, exponential backoff base_ms=200 with jitter reduces client-side queueing. Add async request path avoids blocking UI threads for customers using sync clients.

2026-03-11 03:20 UTC - Root cause hypothesis: A confluence of (1) SDK default pool set to 1 in v1.4.2 for legacy compat, (2) default high retry_attempts with no jitter, and (3) a short-lived increase in 502s from a frontend rolling update. These combined to create a retry cascade that serialized traffic per-client and produced perceived platform slowness for the tenant.
2026-03-11 07:00 UTC - Risk assessment: Any other tenants using the same SDK defaults are at risk under transient errors; customers using async clients or newer SDK versions not affected.
resolution:
Mitigation and fix deployed:
1) Immediate customer workaround: Advised NimbleDocs to update local SDK config: set maxConnections=8, retry_attempts=2, enable jitter (add +/- 20%), and switch to async client where possible. Customer applied changes and confirmed latency returned to baseline.
2) Short-term platform mitigation: SRE adjusted frontend retry gating to be more conservative during rolling updates and added a temporary alert for unusual client-side retry spikes tied to tenant IDs.
3) SDK patch: SDK team published hotfix redwood-sdk-java v1.4.3 (PR #482) which changes default maxConnections to 8 for modern clients, reduces default retry_attempts to 2, and enables jitter in exponential backoff. Patch includes a migration note in CHANGELOG.
4) Long-term actions (planned):
   - Update Quickstart docs and streaming recipes to call out pool sizing and retry settings for high-concurrency streaming workloads.
   - Add a runbook entry to detect and respond to client-side retry cascades, including automated dashboards and an alert on per-tenant retry amplification.
   - Create a telemetry bucket to surface SDK versions associated with high retry amplification and notify Customer Success for outreach.

Ticket status: Leaving this ticket open while customer validates production stability for 72 hours and SDK release propagation is monitored. Follow-ups assigned to SDK and SRE teams (see linked PR and runbook).
